title: Reading the charts cold for Basie at the Adams Theater
summary: Lovett recalls walking in with no rehearsal in Newark, music stacked on Jo Jones's tom-tom; the drum solos were ad lib.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Now the next question that was on this very fine outline submitted by Mr. Taylor of the Performing Arts;

"Describe the change of solo improvising from playing either with written arrangements or in an improvised, Dixie land style?" Perhaps we could substitute the word jazz for Dixie-land in this particular instance. Baby, tell us about the bands -- I know that you're a very, very fine show drummer, therefore, it's also known that you read very well. Tell us --
-- what would you like to hear about it, Art?
Well, now you had to read when you were with Basie. Tell us about that, when you showed up with Basie, about the charts.

Oh, I had no rehearsal at all. We just had to walked in there and played. Jo Jones was drummer, you know, at the time and Basie wired me to come to Newark, New Jersey, the Adams Theater, and I walk in there and the music was all stacked up on Jo Jones' tom tom, you know, and I just had to play the whole show down man without any rehearsal or anything and now that's something very hard to do, I'll tell you that.
If you couldn't read, you couldn't play it so I had to read all the music and everything that was there.
Were the solos written out or were they ad lib? I suppose they were ad lib?
Yeah, the drummer part was ad lib.
